transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2027-04-25
Start time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Alicia (Redwood AE), Mark (Redwood SE), Janelle (Redwood CSM), Sarah (Northstar Procurement), Daniel (Northstar CTO), Priya (Northstar InfoSec), Evan (Northstar Legal)

Summary (auto): Quick procurement and legal alignment on MSA/DPA, confirm SLAs and pricing approval path, discuss onboarding timeline and security requirements. Action items captured.

Transcript:
[00:00] Alicia: hey everyone thanks for joining, um we'll wait just a minute for folks to hop in, but hi Sarah, Daniel, Priya, Evan, thanks for the time
[00:08] Sarah: hey Alicia thanks, we have about 45 minutes, so we'll try and be concise
[00:12] Mark: great, i'll run through the technical bits later, but first wanted to align on the MSA/DPA and SLA asks
[00:18] Daniel: quick note from our side, procurement loop is on a firm timeline - board wants vendor sign-off by first week of May, so we're tight
[00:26] Alicia: understood, that's helpful. our goal today is to make sure legal has what they need and that the pricing path is clear for approvals
[01:10] Evan: okay, i skimmed the MSA and DPA you shared. a couple of high level questions: indemnity limits and data residency language, is there flex on either?
[01:25] Alicia: for indemnity we can discuss, we've had some enterprise customers get limited on a case by case basis, but it's tied to contract tier. data residency - our hosted offering is multi-region, we also support VPC/private deployments for strict residency needs
[02:05] Priya: for InfoSec, the big things are SOC2 attestation, audit logs, KMS integration for key management, and data retention controls in the DPA. do you have a SOC report we can review?
[02:20] Janelle: yes, we can share our SOC2 Type II and our security pack. i'll drop a link after the call, note some of the wording in the DPA is auto-gen so we've seen minor mismatches with customer templates
[03:05] Sarah: also on SLAs - we need clarity on uptime and latency SLOs, and credit structure for breaches. our internal legal wants to see a 99.9% uptime SLA for production-critical endpoints
[03:22] Mark: technically we offer multiple SLA tiers. Hosted standard is 99.9, dedicated pools can go to 99.95 depending on committed capacity and config. the credit calculation is per-month and scaled by affected routes
[03:45] Daniel: latency SLOs - do you guarantee p95 or p99? we have conversational features with tight latency expectations
[03:52] Mark: we typically specify p95 for generation latency on the model profile, p99 is available for dedicated setups with tuned batching and reserved capacity. there is also an option for regional routing to reduce RTT
[04:30] Evan: can you confirm the escalation path and points of contact for SLA incidents? legal wants names and SLAs mapped to contacts
[04:36] Alicia: yes, we'll include a contact matrix. for enterprise we've a designated escalation engineer and an on-call manager, names change but we'll provide role-based contacts plus phone escalation for P1s
[05:10] Priya: about KMS, do you support customer-managed keys (CMK) and HSM integrations? we need to ensure keys never leave our control
[05:18] Mark: we support KMS integrations (AWS KMS/GCP KMS) and have an HSM-backed option for private deployments. for hosted we do envelope encryption with customer-owned keys available for enterprise tiers. note: some low-level logs still have metadata; we can scope those in the DPA
[06:00] Sarah: pricing approvals - our finance team needs committed pricing for the dedicated tier, tiers and any overage rates. can you provide a committed capacity discount matrix?
[06:12] Alicia: yes, our pricing sheet includes on-demand, committed monthly, and annual reserved capacity with unit token prices. we'll send the updated sheet with the discount matrix, also include a sample invoice and billing cadence
[07:05] Daniel: what's typical lead time to stand up a dedicated pool once contract signed? we have an expected go-live window of 3-4 weeks, is that realistic?
[07:15] Mark: for standard dedicated in cloud regions, 2-3 weeks is typical if there's no custom network constraints. VPC/private on-prem can take longer (4-8 weeks) due to networking and security approvals
[07:45] Evan: on the MSA redlines, any clauses we mark for negotiation - do you have standard alternate language you prefer? or should we propose text?
[07:53] Alicia: you can send redlines and we'll respond. for key commercial items we usually have suggested language. for legal, we try to keep it minimal but we can be flexible on indemnity and liability caps depending on contract value
[08:30] Sarah: one blocker is internal procurement needs an explicit data processing clause for our EU customers. your DPA mentions GDPR compliance but we need CSV-like list of subprocessors and data flows
[08:48] Janelle: we have a subprocessors page and a data flow diagram; i'll attach both. note subprocessors change but we maintain a current list and 30 day notice for changes
[09:22] Priya: do you support VPC peering or private link for the hosted product? network isolation is important for us
[09:30] Mark: yes, we support VPC peering and PrivateLink options; private link requires additional networking setup but it's supported for enterprise customers
[10:05] Daniel: curious about the fallback and graceful degradation you mentioned in our earlier demo - how does that interact with dedicated pools and cost?
[10:14] Mark: we have routing policies: primary route hits dedicated pool, fallback routes go to compatible hosted variants which are cheaper but may have different latencies. outages are mitigated by fallback; cost is metered by whichever model handles the request. we can configure hard or soft fallbacks in the routing policy
[11:02] Evan: okay, legal will want explicit language around fallbacks in terms of data handling and logs during fallback events
[11:10] Alicia: yes we'll add clarifying language in the DPA and operational runbook about what gets logged during fallback
[11:48] Sarah: procurement needs an internal sign-off spreadsheet - if you can provide committed pricing and start date, we can route to finance by end of week
[11:56] Alicia: we'll prioritize getting pricing today and send it by end of day tomorrow
[12:28] Mark: on onboarding, typical checklist: account creation, API keys and KMS setup, network peering, test traffic and benchmark run, then cutover. benchmarks usually take 48-72 hours
[12:45] Daniel: can you run a small perf test with our representative prompt set? we'd like to see p95 numbers on our actual workload
[12:52] Mark: yes, we'll do a benchmark. please share the prompt set and expected concurrency, we'll queue a dedicated run in our benchmark cluster
[13:30] Priya: security questionnaire - is there a place to upload answers or will you fill in ours?
[13:36] Janelle: send your questionnaire, we'll fill it and attach SOC reports and architecture diagrams. alternatively we can provide a completed vendor security pack if that helps
[14:05] Evan: about liability cap - would Redwood consider capping liability to contract value or a multiple? our counsel prefers contract value cap
[14:12] Alicia: our standard is usually a multiple of fees paid, but many enterprise deals agree to contract value cap for SaaS; we'll discuss with legal & propose language in response to your redlines
[15:00] Sarah: timeline recap - if we get pricing by 4/26 and provide redlines by 5/3, target signature by 5/7. is that still feasible?
[15:10] Alicia: yes that aligns, assuming no major commercial changes. we'll aim for that cadence
[15:32] Daniel: any special certifications needed for healthcare customers we might have? (we have some health analytics clients)
[15:40] Mark: we have HIPAA-supporting options in private deployments, BAA available. hosted can be HIPAA-eligible with proper contract and config. we'll include BAA template in the packet
[16:05] Priya: encryption in transit and at rest - confirm algorithms and key rotation policies?
[16:12] Mark: TLS1.2+ in transit, AES-256 at rest, support for key rotation via your KMS with yearly rotation by default or custom schedule on private deployments
[16:45] Evan: also want to confirm e-discovery and audit log retention settings in the DPA - we might need longer retention for certain datasets
[16:52] Janelle: retention windows can be configured for enterprise tiers; we'll note the options and default limits in the DPA and show how to request custom retention
[17:30] Sarah: procurement also wants clarity on cancellation and migration assistance - exit plan language in the MSA
[17:38] Alicia: standard exit assistance is 90 days support and data export options; extended migration packages are available as a paid add-on
[18:05] Daniel: any network egress costs we should anticipate during migration or heavy usage months?
[18:12] Alicia: egress is billed according to region and cloud provider prices, we'll include estimates in the pricing sheet and can add a sample invoice showing egress lines
[18:48] Priya: one more Q from security - do you perform pen tests and will we get a summary of findings? are third-party pen tests shared?
[18:56] Mark: we do regular pen tests and will share an executive summary; detailed reports are shared under NDA, but SOC and summary info is standard
[19:30] Evan: sounds good. legal will prepare redlines and route internally. smallest ask: include an explicit subprocessors list and contact for data protection questions
[19:38] Janelle: noted, i'll attach subprocessors list and DPO contact in the packet
[20:15] Sarah: last thing on pricing governance - we need a fixed price period for reserved capacity for at least 12 months to avoid surprise price changes
[20:24] Alicia: we can offer price protection for committed annual terms; we'll include protective language in the commercial terms section
[21:05] Daniel: ok, that covers most of my concerns. Mark, please confirm the p99 option and cost delta for dedicated
[21:12] Mark: p99 guaranteed for dedicated with tuned config; cost delta depends on model and concurrency, typical uplift 10-30% over standard p95 SLA - will call out specifics in the pricing spreadsheet
[22:00] Alicia: to recap next steps: we send pricing + SLA table by 4/26, SE shares benchmark run instructions and runbook by 4/27, Northstar to provide redlines by 5/03, schedule signature readiness call 5/07. Any objections?
[22:12] Sarah: none from procurement, thanks
[22:20] Priya: sounds good from security
[22:26] Evan: legal okay
[22:30] Alicia: great, we'll follow up with the packet and links. thanks everyone
[22:45] Meeting end

Shared artifacts/links referenced: Pricing sheet (to be sent), SOC2 report link (to be sent), subprocessors list, onboarding runbook, benchmark spreadsheet (SE to share), BAA template (to be attached).

Notes about transcription: occasional misheard words and speaker overlaps, timestamps approximate.
